original_question: Under what condition on the holonomy of a compact leaf L in a C 0 transversally oriented foliation of codimension > 1, the leaf L is stable?
target_in_paper: Question 3.19 in Section 3.6, "Amenable actions and planar groups and the Euler class" (page 13). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact problem the paper asks: a compact leaf L of a C^0 transversally oriented foliation, codimension > 1, and the search for holonomy conditions that force stability. This is essentially the wording of Question 3.19. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: The official target is not a theorem or conjecture but Question 3.19 in Section 3.6. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The paper states the problem for a compact leaf L of a C^0 transversally oriented foliation F, so naming the foliation and the leaf explicitly makes the question stand alone. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The paper also includes a specific codimension-2 test case, which your draft omits: F is a C^0 codimension 2 foliation and L is a compact leaf. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

In that codimension-2 test case, the normal microbundle of L is assumed to have trivial Euler class. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
The same test case also assumes that the fundamental group pi_1(L) is amenable. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The cohomological hypothesis H^1(L; R) = 0 is part of the paper's explicit example and is missing from the draft; the coefficient field is R. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The draft leaves the intended notion of "stable" implicit; the nearby context shows the question is framed in the Reeb/Thurston local-stability setting, motivated by whether L has a product-type foliated neighborhood in the codimension-one amenable case. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

No extra algebraic data such as degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers appear in this problem; the essential missing content is geometric/topological rather than algebraic. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Determine the higher-codimension C^0 analogue of Thurston-type stability asked in the paper: if F is a C^0 transversally oriented foliation of codimension q > 1 and L is a compact leaf, what condition on the holonomy of L guarantees that L is stable? In particular, if q = 2, F is a C^0 codimension-2 foliation, the normal microbundle of L has trivial Euler class, pi_1(L) is amenable, and H^1(L; R) = 0, must L be stable? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: This refinement stays as close as possible to the paper because it is just Question 3.19 rewritten with the notation and hypotheses made explicit. The paragraph immediately before Question 3.19 explains the intended scope: it is motivated by Thurston's C^0 codimension-one stability conjecture for compact leaves with amenable fundamental group and vanishing H^1(L; R), and then asks for the corresponding higher-codimension holonomy criterion, highlighting the codimension-2 case with trivial Euler class of the normal microbundle. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
